evidence: Caes. BG 4.1.9: nūllō officiō aut disciplīnā assuēfactī (Lewis & Short)

terms.comment: Exāctor, an enforcer or overseer, is classical (Livy, Quintilian: assiduus studiōrum exāctor, Lewis & Short); feminine exāctrīx (Traupman). Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

sources: Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 304.
